_comment: M_E refers to Earth Masses, 5.972E24 kg. R_E refers to Earth Radius, 6371 km
_comment_mass_bounds: M_E_min/M_E_max are the mass draw bounds. Rocky mass is drawn before the subclass is known, so it uses terrestrial M_E_min to super_earth M_E_max; the subclass then follows from the mass. Giant mass is re-clamped to its subclass after the metallicity/star-mass/competition modifiers; rocky and dwarf mass is not, so modifiers can push it slightly outside these bounds.
_comment_radius_model: R = radius_reference.radius * (M / radius_reference.mass) ^ s, with s drawn from radius_exponent_range. Without radius_reference the law is Earth-anchored (R = M^s). radius_scatter, if present, multiplies the result. Above inflated_mass_min the radius is drawn from inflated_radius_range instead. The result is clamped to R_E_min/R_E_max.

rocky._comment_mass: Sub-Earth (< 0.1 Me) is treated as the low end of this class, not a separate subclass.
rocky._comment_moon: Terrestrial bodies rarely have moons. 0-1 with low probability.
rocky._comment_stripping: Stellar stripping modifier — sub-Earths (< 0.1 Me) are more vulnerable.
rocky._comment_tidal: Rocky body moons are rocky by default — small captured bodies or impact debris.

rocky._comment_mass: Above 2 Me gravity regime shifts meaningfully. Upper bound 20 Me caps the rocky mass draw.
rocky._comment_moon: Super-Earths can capture or retain small moons.
rocky._comment_amf: Super-Earths have stronger outgassing — boost atmosphere mass fraction.
rocky._comment_volcanic: Higher internal heat — nudge volcanic activity up one tier.
rocky._comment_tidal: Rocky body moons are rocky by default — small captured bodies or impact debris.

giant._comment_mass: Saturn ~95 Me, Jupiter ~318 Me. 30-95 Me overlaps ice_giant: sub-Saturns, assigned by the sigmoid in assign_giant_subclass. Bodies below M_E_min are always ice_giant.
giant._comment_radius: Anchored to Saturn. R_E_min 6.0 lets sub-Saturns down to 30 Me land ~6.8-7.8 Re unclamped. Above inflated_mass_min, radius is drawn flat (inflated Jupiters).
giant._comment_gas_table: Weights are relative, not fractions. H2-dominant per real gas giant composition. Fixes He/H2 inversion bug.
giant._comment_dynamo: Gas giants have deep metallic hydrogen layers driving strong dynamos.
giant._comment_moon: Gas giant moon counts: Jovian-class up to 12, Saturn-class toward lower end of range.
giant._comment_tidal: k2 = Love number (interior deformability). Q = tidal dissipation factor (efficiency of heat conversion). Rocky moons dissipate efficiently, icy moons poorly but insulate subsurface oceans.

rocky_moon._comment: Io-like. Low Q = efficient dissipation = high heat output.

icy_moon._comment: Europa/Ganymede-like. High Q = inefficient dissipation but ice insulates subsurface ocean.

giant._comment_ice_line_proxy: Moon type threshold: moons within this fraction of parent SMA are rocky, beyond are icy. Mirrors planetary ice line logic.

giant._comment_mass: Uranus ~14.5 Me, Neptune ~17 Me. Upper bound 95 Me: bodies at or above it are always gas_giant. 30-95 Me overlaps gas_giant.
giant._comment_gas_table: Ice giants are water/methane/ammonia mantle bodies with thin H2/He envelope. CH4 gives Uranus/Neptune blue-green color.
giant._comment_dynamo: Ice giants have weaker, less organised dynamos than gas giants — Uranus/Neptune both irregular.
giant._comment_moon: Ice giants have fewer and smaller moons than gas giants.
